Let
\[
e_m(u)=\exp(2\pi i u/2^m).
\]
We use the standard quadratic Gauss sum
\[
G_m(a)=\sum_{x\bmod 2^m} e_m(x^2-ax).
\]
For \(m\ge2\),
\[
G_m(a)=0\quad(a\text{ odd}),
\]
and if \(a=2b\),
\[
G_m(2b)=g_m e_m(-b^2),\qquad g_m=\sum_x e_m(x^2)=2^{m/2}(1+i).
\]

Sum first over \(z\). It is nonzero only when \(y+t\) is even. Write
\[
y=2u-t,\qquad u\bmod 2^{m-1}.
\]
Then summing over \(x\) is nonzero only when \(r-t\) is even. Put
\[
d=\frac{r-t}{2}\bmod 2^{m-1}.
\]
The remaining \(u\)-sum is nonzero only when
\[
s+d\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
Write
\[
q=\frac{s+d}{2}\bmod 2^{m-1}.
\]
For every nonzero case,
\[
A_m(r,s,t)=g_m^2g_{m-1}
\exp\left(2\pi i\left(\frac{C-2e^2}{2^m}\right)\right),
\]
where
\[
e=t+q,\qquad C=t^2+st-d^2.
\]
Since
\[
g_m^2g_{m-1}
\]
has argument \(3\pi/4\), the sign is controlled by
\[
H=C-2e^2.
\]
A direct simplification gives
\[
H=-J(t,d,q),
\]
where
\[
J(t,d,q)=t^2+td+d^2+2qt+2q^2.
\]

Thus \(A_m\) is positive real exactly when
\[
H\equiv 5\cdot 2^{m-3}\pmod{2^m},
\]
and negative real exactly when
\[
H\equiv 2^{m-3}\pmod{2^m}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
J\equiv 3\cdot 2^{m-3}\pmod{2^m}
\]
for positive values, and
\[
J\equiv 7\cdot 2^{m-3}\pmod{2^m}
\]
for negative values.

The quadratic form \(J\) has the key scaling property: if
\[
J\equiv c2^{n-3}\pmod{2^n},\qquad c\text{ odd},
\]
then for \(n\ge5\), all variables are even, and dividing by \(4\) gives the same counting problem modulo \(2^{n-2}\), with a factor \(8\) from the free high bits.

The base residue counts are:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
n & c=1 & c=3 & c=5 & c=7\\ \hline
3 & 96 & 96 & 96 & 96\\
4 & 192 & 128 & 192 & 0
\end{array}
\]
with the separate \(m=4\) count giving \(P_4=32,\ N_4=0\).

Therefore:

- If \(m\) is odd,
\[
P_m=N_m=3\cdot 2^{(3m-3)/2}.
\]

- If \(m\) is even,
\[
P_m=2^{(3m-2)/2},\qquad N_m=0.
\]

So the final answer is
\[
\boxed{
(P_m,N_m)=
\begin{cases}
\left(2^{(3m-2)/2},\,0\right), & m\text{ even},\\[4pt]
\left(3\cdot 2^{(3m-3)/2},\,3\cdot 2^{(3m-3)/2}\right), & m\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]
